SpaceX snapped up low-band spectrum in a bid to take on T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

SpaceX has acquired a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses — a move the company says “will pave the way” for its Starlink Mobile service to become a “major” US carrier. When the Federal Communications Commission signs off on the deal, SpaceX says it will deploy its new architecture that combines its satellite-to-mobile constellation with a terrestrial mobile network, directly competing with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

The licenses include up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, which SpaceX says will allow Starlink Mobile’s signal to penetrate through walls and buildings. SpaceX previously acquired 2GHz spectrum from EchoStar as part of efforts to bolster its direct-to-device service.

The FCC has also approved plans to deploy 15,000 V2 Starlink Mobile satellites that will offer more than 100 times the bandwidth than the current generation, according to SpaceX. “With this new low-band spectrum and our Gen2 constellation, Starlink Mobile can now become the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum,” SpaceX says. “One network that provides Americans with a reliable service indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.”

financeStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

But will existing handhelds get the tech?

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Sean Hollister

It’s already possible to get AMD’s framerate-enhancing FSR 4 boost on handhelds as old as the Steam Deck — but in June, AMD reserved the right to disappoint handheld gamers by not officially bringing FSR 4 to older handhelds. Now, AMD consumer chip boss Jack Huynh says he will bring the tech to some handhelds by the end of the year.

Which handhelds? It’s still not clear if it will come to existing handhelds, or if you’ll need a new one to get it — because it comes alongside news that AMD is releasing a new FSR4-capable chip.

“We will expand the machine learning AI-based FSR4 technology, which was first introduced to existing external graphics cards, to the entire product line including APUs, gaming laptops, and handheld devices by the end of this year,” Huynh told Korean publication The Elec (via Google Translate). “We plan to respond in two directions: launching existing APUs and new product lines.”

The Elec says that means both a new APU, and a lightweight FSR4 model for APUs, are coming by year’s end. (Previously, AMD had only promised FSR4 for desktop graphics cards, not APUs bound for laptops and handhelds.) But The Elec doesn’t seem to say if that lightweight FSR4 model is coming to handhelds specifically. Perhaps it’ll require AMD’s leaked upcoming Ryzen Z3 and/or “Gainsborough” handheld chips.

Back when AMD threw a little cold water on the idea of FSR 4 for existing handhelds, exec David McAfee told Tom’s Guide that “we want to make sure the experience and the quality is right” and that AMD would need “a sufficient amount of compute within that product” for FSR 4 to make sense. Perhaps some older laptop chips will qualify, while some older handheld chips don’t.

Valve worked with AMD to bring FSR 4 to the Steam Machine’s console-grade AMD APU, but it hasn’t yet committed to the same for the Steam Deck handhelds.

AMD didn’t immediately respond to a request to clarify Huynh’s statement.

尽管像Steam Deck这样较早期的掌机已经有可能获得AMD提升帧率的FSR 4技术加持——但在今年6月，AMD并未承诺正式将FSR 4带给较旧的掌机，保留了让掌机玩家失望的可能。如今，AMD消费级芯片业务负责人杰克·黄（Jack Huynh）表示，他将在今年年底前把这项技术引入部分掌机设备。

具体是哪些掌机？目前尚不清楚它是否会支持现有的掌机，还是需要购买新设备才能获得——因为这一消息伴随着AMD即将发布支持FSR 4的新芯片的新闻一同传出。

“我们将在今年年底前，把最初引入现有独立显卡的基于机器学习AI的FSR 4技术，扩展到包括APU、游戏笔记本和掌机设备在内的整个产品线，”黄向韩国媒体The Elec表示（经由谷歌翻译）。“我们计划从两个方向推进：兼顾现有APU并推出新产品线。”

The Elec报道称，这意味着一款新APU以及针对APU的轻量级FSR 4模型都将在今年年底前推出。（此前，AMD仅承诺将FSR 4用于桌面独立显卡，而非面向笔记本和掌机的APU。）但The Elec似乎并未明确说明该轻量级FSR 4模型是否会专门登陆掌机。或许它需要AMD此前被泄露的即将推出的Ryzen Z3和/或“Gainsborough”掌机芯片。

此前在AMD给现有掌机支持FSR 4的设想泼冷水时，高管戴维·麦卡菲（David McAfee）曾对《汤姆硬件指南》（Tom’s Guide）表示，“我们希望确保体验和画质达到标准”，并且AMD需要“该产品具备足够的算力”才能让FSR 4发挥实际意义。也许一些较旧的笔记本芯片能够满足条件，而部分较旧的掌机芯片则不行。

Valve曾与AMD合作将FSR 4引入Steam Machine的主机级AMD APU，但尚未承诺对Steam Deck掌机采取同样举措。

AMD未立即回应置评请求以澄清黄的言论。

financeStories.originalTitle: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
financeStories.snippet: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through the Theranos founder's desk.
financeStories.fullContent:
With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents unveiled during the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to be the chief executive of Theranos before everything came crashing down.

(Every day, I am grateful to the American legal system for making the discovery process public.)

i built a website where you can sit at elizabeth holmes’ deskopen her macbook, scroll her iphone, run the theranos edison machineher texts, emails, slides, documents, and theranos machine records are real, sourced from exhibits in the united states v. holmes criminal trial pic.twitter.com/5At9T5m3UV

The environment that Lau created is ambitiously detailed, taking you right back to 2016, a time when iPhones had home buttons, and you had to slide your finger across the screen to unlock it. Even the MacBook Air is running OS X El Capitan.

You can click around the environment, which lets you look through the documents made public from the court case on Holmes’ iPhone and laptop screens. You can even run the Theranos Edison machine, the company’s ill-fated device that was supposed to be able to extract large amounts of health data from one drop of blood.

The project seems like it was mostly made for laughs, but it’s actually an interesting way to peruse the documents from one of the most infamous court cases in tech history — it’s a lot easier to navigate this than to source thousands of PDFs from court websites.

There’s another agenda, though. Lau is promoting a watch party that her company is throwing for Nathan Fielder’s upcoming documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, “You Can See Everything.”

Also, of course, she’s promoting the company itself. So, what exactly does Extend do? Apparently, it can “parse, extract, and split your hardest documents with unmatched accuracy.” (I’m not really sure what that means, but if it makes something like this Holmes desk simulator possible, then I guess that means I’m bullish on B2B SaaS.)

（每天，我都要感谢美国法律体系让证据开示过程向公众公开。）
我建了一个网站，你可以坐在伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的办公桌前，打开她的 MacBook，滑动她的 iPhone，运行 Theranos Edison 仪器。她的短信、邮件、幻灯片、文件和 Theranos 仪器记录都是真实的，来源于美国诉霍姆斯刑事审判案中的证据材料 pic.twitter.com/5At9T5m3UV
Lau 打造的环境极其注重细节，直接将你带回 2016 年——那个 iPhone 还有 Home 键、需要滑动手指解锁屏幕的时代。就连 MacBook Air 运行的也是 OS X El Capitan 系统。
你可以在这个环境中随意点击，通过霍姆斯的 iPhone 和笔记本屏幕查阅庭审中公开的文件。你甚至还可以运行 Theranos Edison 仪器——该公司命运多舛的设备，据称本应能够仅凭一滴血提取海量健康数据。
这个项目看起来大多是为了找乐子，但它实际上也是细细查阅科技史上最臭名昭著的案件文件的一种有趣方式——浏览这个网站，可比从法院网站上调取成千上万份 PDF 要轻松得多。
不过，这背后还有另一个目的。Lau 正在宣传其公司即将为内森·菲尔德（Nathan Fielder）关于伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的新纪录片《你能看清一切》（You Can See Everything）举办的观影派对。

aiStories.title: Sophos 借助 OpenAI Daybreak 将威胁调查时间缩短 96%
aiStories.originalTitle: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
aiStories.snippet: Discover how Sophos uses OpenAI’s Daybreak to cut cyber-threat investigation time by 96% and automate 52% of MDR cases while preserving human oversight.
aiStories.fullContent:
With OpenAI Daybreak, Sophos combines frontier intelligence with cybersecurity expertise to investigate threats faster and protect customers at scale.

average response time for cases using AI agents

reduction in investigation time using OpenAI models

of MDR cases resolved end-to-end by AI

Frontier AI is changing cybersecurity on both sides⁠(opens in a new window). Advanced models can help defenders find and investigate threats faster. But those capabilities are also spreading to open-weight models, giving attackers new ways to discover vulnerabilities and accelerate exploitation.

Sophos⁠(opens in a new window) is one of the companies standing in their way, protecting more than 625,000 organisations across sectors and regions. “We see a huge variety of different attacks,” says John Peterson, the company’s Chief Technology Officer. “We’ve cultivated vast expertise in combating them over four decades in the cybersecurity business.”

Through OpenAI Daybreak, Sophos is combining OpenAI models with its own threat intelligence, response playbooks and security expertise. The aim isn’t simply to give analysts another tool. It’s to increase the impact of Sophos’s expertise across every customer it protects.

“Sophos brings the domain expertise and the know-how to combat attacks at scale. Programmes like Daybreak, and companies like OpenAI, bring frontier intelligence that allows us to take that domain expertise and scale it to support all of our customers.”

At the centre of the work is Sophos Fusion, the Sophos AI-native cyber defense system that includes Sophos Managed Detection and Response (MDR). It brings together sensor data from more than 500 third-party integrations alongside Sophos’s own products. Together, those sensors generate trillions of events every day, which Sophos distills into roughly 1,000 to 2,000 cases for its nine security operations centres to investigate.

Agents built through Daybreak have changed how those cases are handled. An investigation agent gathers the customer context, detections, indicators of compromise (IoCs) and relevant threat intelligence for each case. A planning model then creates a plan–execute–review loop: building an investigation plan, completing the steps and producing a summary with recommended response actions for analysts to review. Other agents can carry out parts of the response.

Before Daybreak, investigating and responding to a case depended primarily on human expertise. Sophos’s existing process averaged around 38 minutes — performance Peterson says was better than 96% of professional security operations centres.

“Now, because of the agents we’ve been able to build through the Daybreak programme, the average response time for cases using those agents has fallen to about 89 seconds. About half of the cases we handle are now being automated by agents we developed using the Daybreak models.”

Sophos has built customer control into its MDR service through three operating modes:

Notify: Sophos investigates the case and recommends a response, but the customer acts.

Collaborate: Sophos and the customer work together before action is taken.

Authorise: Sophos can respond directly on the customer’s behalf.

The same boundaries apply whether work is completed by a person or an agent. Sophos uses automation to move quickly and make better use of analysts’ time, but potentially destructive actions still require the right level of human oversight.

“Anything we don’t feel comfortable with an agent handling gets passed off for human judgement,” Peterson confirms.

Reduced the average response time for cases using agents from approximately 38 minutes to 89 seconds.

Enabled Sophos to resolve 52% of MDR cases end-to-end with AI, within boundaries calibrated by Sophos analysts.

Gives customers a faster and more consistent investigation experience.

Helps Sophos scale compute rather than relying on equivalent growth in scarce cybersecurity headcount.

Returns analysts’ attention to the threats, exceptions and decisions where their expertise matters most.

Peterson says Sophos will keep expanding what its agents can do. “The response capabilities are going to continue to become more sophisticated, and we’re going to broaden the range of use cases we address with the agents we’ve built.”

“With programmes like Daybreak, we have an opportunity to stay a step ahead of the attacker community.”

His advice for other security leaders is simple: “The one thing security leaders should do tomorrow is really come back to focusing on the security fundamentals for their organization,” he says. “That of course includes patching. But patches are only ever going to include vulnerabilities that are known by the vendor.”

The answer is to maintain “a layered security approach” that includes endpoint protection, multifactor authentication (MFA), network segmentation and strong security operations. “Vulnerabilities are being discovered at an alarming rate and exploited at a scale that we’ve never seen. So I think doing the fundamentals well is more important today than it’s ever been.”
aiStories.fullTranslation:
借助 OpenAI Daybreak，Sophos 将前沿智能与网络安全专业能力相结合，能够更快地调查威胁并在规模化层面上保护客户。
使用 AI 智能体案例的平均响应时间
使用 OpenAI 模型缩短的调查时间
由 AI 端到端解决的 MDR 案例比例
前沿 AI 正在深刻改变攻防两端。先进的模型能够协助防御者更快地发现并调查威胁。但这些能力也正扩散至开源权重模型中，为攻击者提供了发现漏洞和加速利用的新途径。
Sophos 是阻挡这些攻击的企业之一，为各行各业以及各个地区的逾 62.5 万家机构提供安全防护。“我们见识过种类极其繁多的攻击，”该公司首席技术官约翰·彼得森（John Peterson）表示，“在长达 40 年的网络安全业务历程中，我们积累了极为深厚的对抗经验。”
通过 OpenAI Daybreak，Sophos 将 OpenAI 的模型与其自身的威胁情报、响应处置手册（playbooks）及安全专业知识相结合。其目标不仅仅是为分析师提供又一个工具，而是要放大 Sophos 专业能力在所保护的每位客户身上的实际效能。
“Sophos 拥有大规模抵御攻击的领域专业知识和实战诀窍。像 Daybreak 这样的项目以及像 OpenAI 这样的公司，带来了前沿智能，使我们能够将这一领域专长进行规模化扩展，从而支持所有客户。”
这项工作的核心是 Sophos Fusion——这是包含 Sophos 托管检测与响应（MDR）在内的 Sophos AI 原生网络防御系统。它汇集了来自 500 多个第三方集成组件以及 Sophos 自身产品的传感器数据。这些传感器每天共同生成数万亿次事件，Sophos 将其提炼为约 1,000 至 2,000 个案例，供其九个安全运营中心进行调查。
通过 Daybreak 构建的智能体（Agents）改变了这些案例的处置方式。一个调查智能体负责为每个案例收集客户背景、检测数据、失陷指标（IoCs）以及相关威胁情报。随后，规划模型建立起一个“规划-执行-复核”闭环：制定调查计划、完成执行步骤，并生成包含建议响应操作的摘要，供分析人员审核。其他智能体则可以执行部分响应操作。
在引入 Daybreak 之前，调查和响应案例主要依赖人工专长。Sophos 先前的流程平均耗时约 38 分钟——彼得森表示，这一表现已优于 96% 的专业安全运营中心。
“现在，得益于我们通过 Daybreak 项目构建的智能体，使用这些智能体的案例平均响应时间已降至约 89 秒。我们处置的案例中约有一半现在正由利用 Daybreak 模型开发的智能体实现自动化处理。”
Sophos 通过三种运行模式将客户控制权内嵌到其 MDR 服务中：
通知（Notify）：Sophos 负责调查案例并建议应对措施，但由客户采取行动。
协作（Collaborate）：Sophos 与客户在采取行动前共同协作配合。
授权（Authorise）：Sophos 可直接代表客户采取应对措施。
无论工作是由人工完成还是由智能体完成，均适用相同的边界规则。Sophos 利用自动化提高敏捷性并更高效地利用分析师的时间，但潜在具有破坏性的操作仍需要适度的人工监督。
“任何我们认为让智能体处置不放心的事项，都会转交由人工判断，”彼得森证实道。
将使用智能体的案例平均响应时间从约 38 分钟缩短至 89 秒。
使 Sophos 能够在分析师校准的边界内，通过 AI 端到端解决 52% 的 MDR 案例。
为客户提供更快、更一致的调查体验。
协助 Sophos 实现算力规模化扩展，而非单纯依赖等量扩充稀缺的网络安全人力资源。
让分析人员的注意力重新回归到最需要其专业知识的威胁、异常情况和决策制定上。
彼得森表示，Sophos 将继续拓展其智能体的能力范畴。“响应能力将变得越来越成熟完备，并且我们将利用所构建的智能体进一步拓宽所涵盖的应用场景范围。”
“借助像 Daybreak 这样的项目，我们有机会领先攻击者群体一步。”
对于其他安全负责人的建议，他给出的解答十分明确：“安全负责人明天最该做的一件事，就是真正重新把重心放在本组织的安全基础工作上，”他表示，“这当然包括打补丁。但补丁永远只能覆盖厂商已知的漏洞。”
答案在于保持“分层安全防御方法”，包括端点保护、多因素认证（MFA）、网络分段以及健全的安全运营。“漏洞正以惊人的速度被发现，并以前所未有的规模被利用。因此我认为，在当下把基础工作做好比以往任何时候都更加关键。”

Friday, October 16, 2026

Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Join senior AI reporter James O’Donnell as he interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology.

Going live on October 16th at 18:30 BST / 1:30pm EDT / 10:30am PDT

Speakers : James O’Donnell , AI Reporter, and Samuel King , Bioengineering PhD Candidate, Stanford University/Arc Institute

He asked an AI to design viruses … and it worked.

AI-designed viruses are here and already killing bacteria

2026年10月16日，星期五

aiStories.originalTitle: President Trump awards Big Tech donors with nation’s highest science prizes
aiStories.snippet: Together, the awardees have donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration.
aiStories.fullContent:
On Thursday, at the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit, President Trump awarded Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD’s Lisa Su the National Medal of Science, the nation’s top science prize. Dell Technologies’ Michael Dell and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella also received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

Together, the awardees have donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration, according to The New Republic. Alphabet and Microsoft, for example, donated to the president’s inauguration fund and White House ballroom. AMD gave to a pro-Trump Super PAC, and Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to help fund the Trump Accounts, the administration’s savings program for children.

Trump said the honorees had helped “pioneer an incredible future for America,” and that because of them, “we will always be on top. No one else can compete with us.”

Nadella received his medal right after the administration indefinitely suspended Microsoft from the H-1B program, which lets U.S. companies hire skilled foreign workers.

The United States’ execution of the Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed, anonymous officials from the Defense Department told the BBC and Associated Press. The planned execution of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major convicted of killing 13 people at the Texas military base, was announced this week. He is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3rd at 2PM ET.

The Verge contacted YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Meta, Rumble, and Kick to ask if they plan to allow the livestream to be aired on their platforms. None responded before publication.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in an interview with Real America’s Voice.

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The new OSS Scanner service offers vulnerability reports from Anthropic’s “strongest models,” including Mythos.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Stevie Bonifield

Anthropic’s offering to help open-source projects track down security vulnerabilities with a new service called OSS Scanner. It says open-source projects that opt-in will get “thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.” That could mean open-source projects get alerted about possible security issues sooner, but the trade-off is that OSS Scanner’s reports don’t come with human review:

The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage. This will enable faster and more frequent scanning, but means that it is possible reports will be incorrect or invalid. These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos) to give open-source projects the largest defensive advantage.

OSS Scanner is far from the first AI bug hunting helper out there. AI tools have helped find some major security flaws in open-source software over recent months, like the “Copy Fail” bug that impacted nearly every Linux distro in May. At the same time, some open-source projects are struggling to keep up with the sudden onslaught of AI-generated bug reports, including Linus Torvalds and even Google.

aiStories.fullContent:

SpaceX snapped up low-band spectrum in a bid to take on T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

SpaceX has acquired a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses — a move the company says “will pave the way” for its Starlink Mobile service to become a “major” US carrier. When the Federal Communications Commission signs off on the deal, SpaceX says it will deploy its new architecture that combines its satellite-to-mobile constellation with a terrestrial mobile network, directly competing with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

The licenses include up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, which SpaceX says will allow Starlink Mobile’s signal to penetrate through walls and buildings. SpaceX previously acquired 2GHz spectrum from EchoStar as part of efforts to bolster its direct-to-device service.

The FCC has also approved plans to deploy 15,000 V2 Starlink Mobile satellites that will offer more than 100 times the bandwidth than the current generation, according to SpaceX. “With this new low-band spectrum and our Gen2 constellation, Starlink Mobile can now become the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum,” SpaceX says. “One network that provides Americans with a reliable service indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.”

aiStories.fullContent:

But will existing handhelds get the tech?

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Sean Hollister

It’s already possible to get AMD’s framerate-enhancing FSR 4 boost on handhelds as old as the Steam Deck — but in June, AMD reserved the right to disappoint handheld gamers by not officially bringing FSR 4 to older handhelds. Now, AMD consumer chip boss Jack Huynh says he will bring the tech to some handhelds by the end of the year.

Which handhelds? It’s still not clear if it will come to existing handhelds, or if you’ll need a new one to get it — because it comes alongside news that AMD is releasing a new FSR4-capable chip.

“We will expand the machine learning AI-based FSR4 technology, which was first introduced to existing external graphics cards, to the entire product line including APUs, gaming laptops, and handheld devices by the end of this year,” Huynh told Korean publication The Elec (via Google Translate). “We plan to respond in two directions: launching existing APUs and new product lines.”

The Elec says that means both a new APU, and a lightweight FSR4 model for APUs, are coming by year’s end. (Previously, AMD had only promised FSR4 for desktop graphics cards, not APUs bound for laptops and handhelds.) But The Elec doesn’t seem to say if that lightweight FSR4 model is coming to handhelds specifically. Perhaps it’ll require AMD’s leaked upcoming Ryzen Z3 and/or “Gainsborough” handheld chips.

Back when AMD threw a little cold water on the idea of FSR 4 for existing handhelds, exec David McAfee told Tom’s Guide that “we want to make sure the experience and the quality is right” and that AMD would need “a sufficient amount of compute within that product” for FSR 4 to make sense. Perhaps some older laptop chips will qualify, while some older handheld chips don’t.

Valve worked with AMD to bring FSR 4 to the Steam Machine’s console-grade AMD APU, but it hasn’t yet committed to the same for the Steam Deck handhelds.

AMD didn’t immediately respond to a request to clarify Huynh’s statement.

尽管像Steam Deck这样较早期的掌机已经有可能获得AMD提升帧率的FSR 4技术加持——但在今年6月，AMD并未承诺正式将FSR 4带给较旧的掌机，保留了让掌机玩家失望的可能。如今，AMD消费级芯片业务负责人杰克·黄（Jack Huynh）表示，他将在今年年底前把这项技术引入部分掌机设备。

具体是哪些掌机？目前尚不清楚它是否会支持现有的掌机，还是需要购买新设备才能获得——因为这一消息伴随着AMD即将发布支持FSR 4的新芯片的新闻一同传出。

“我们将在今年年底前，把最初引入现有独立显卡的基于机器学习AI的FSR 4技术，扩展到包括APU、游戏笔记本和掌机设备在内的整个产品线，”黄向韩国媒体The Elec表示（经由谷歌翻译）。“我们计划从两个方向推进：兼顾现有APU并推出新产品线。”

The Elec报道称，这意味着一款新APU以及针对APU的轻量级FSR 4模型都将在今年年底前推出。（此前，AMD仅承诺将FSR 4用于桌面独立显卡，而非面向笔记本和掌机的APU。）但The Elec似乎并未明确说明该轻量级FSR 4模型是否会专门登陆掌机。或许它需要AMD此前被泄露的即将推出的Ryzen Z3和/或“Gainsborough”掌机芯片。

此前在AMD给现有掌机支持FSR 4的设想泼冷水时，高管戴维·麦卡菲（David McAfee）曾对《汤姆硬件指南》（Tom’s Guide）表示，“我们希望确保体验和画质达到标准”，并且AMD需要“该产品具备足够的算力”才能让FSR 4发挥实际意义。也许一些较旧的笔记本芯片能够满足条件，而部分较旧的掌机芯片则不行。

Valve曾与AMD合作将FSR 4引入Steam Machine的主机级AMD APU，但尚未承诺对Steam Deck掌机采取同样举措。

AMD未立即回应置评请求以澄清黄的言论。

aiStories.originalTitle: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
aiStories.snippet: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through the Theranos founder's desk.
aiStories.fullContent:
With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents unveiled during the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to be the chief executive of Theranos before everything came crashing down.

(Every day, I am grateful to the American legal system for making the discovery process public.)

i built a website where you can sit at elizabeth holmes’ deskopen her macbook, scroll her iphone, run the theranos edison machineher texts, emails, slides, documents, and theranos machine records are real, sourced from exhibits in the united states v. holmes criminal trial pic.twitter.com/5At9T5m3UV

The environment that Lau created is ambitiously detailed, taking you right back to 2016, a time when iPhones had home buttons, and you had to slide your finger across the screen to unlock it. Even the MacBook Air is running OS X El Capitan.

You can click around the environment, which lets you look through the documents made public from the court case on Holmes’ iPhone and laptop screens. You can even run the Theranos Edison machine, the company’s ill-fated device that was supposed to be able to extract large amounts of health data from one drop of blood.

The project seems like it was mostly made for laughs, but it’s actually an interesting way to peruse the documents from one of the most infamous court cases in tech history — it’s a lot easier to navigate this than to source thousands of PDFs from court websites.

There’s another agenda, though. Lau is promoting a watch party that her company is throwing for Nathan Fielder’s upcoming documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, “You Can See Everything.”

Also, of course, she’s promoting the company itself. So, what exactly does Extend do? Apparently, it can “parse, extract, and split your hardest documents with unmatched accuracy.” (I’m not really sure what that means, but if it makes something like this Holmes desk simulator possible, then I guess that means I’m bullish on B2B SaaS.)

aiStories.fullContent:
Preparing CAD assets for robotics simulation requires more than converting geometry to OpenUSD: developers must configure and validate materials, collision geometry, joints, and other physics properties before testing robot behavior.

NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, guided by SimReady Foundation specifications and agentic NVIDIA skills, provide a structured workflow for converting and validating simulation ready (SimReady) assets. Frontier AI models can assist developers at each stage by interpreting reference materials and calling Omniverse tools on their behalf, reducing manual preparation.

This post walks through how to prepare an ABB Robotics YuMi robot for simulation using the SimReady Foundation and NVIDIA Omniverse tools, with GPT-6 Astra as one example of a frontier AI model that can assist with the process. The workflow covers five steps: STEP-file conversion, appearance validation, physics configuration, SimReady validation, and a final pick-and-place task with both arms and grippers in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

SimReady defines requirements for preparing OpenUSD assets for specific simulation use cases. Developers select a SimReady profile for their intended use and validate the asset against its requirements. Profile-specific checks validate the asset’s structure, materials, and physics properties, then flag issues for developers to fix and recheck.

A robot model can look correct but still fail in simulation if it is missing simulation properties. For example, missing collision geometry can allow objects to pass through its gripper and incorrect joints can prevent coordinated motion. Simulation properties like mass and friction directly affect whether a grasp remains stable.

The following technologies and tools support this workflow:

This walkthrough demonstrates the five-step SimReady workflow using an ABB Yumi robot. GPT-6 Astra is used here as one example of a frontier AI model that can help write Python code to call NVIDIA Omniverse libraries at each stage, but the workflow can be applied across many models and robot systems.

The example uses both arms and grippers, configured during the workflow. Cubes and a Sharpie marker were used as demonstrations in step 5. Camera-based perception can be added in a separate workflow.

In this workflow example, we used Isaac Sim 6.1 and Codex CLI and launched Isaac Sim in windowed mode.

Use the following example prompt in your active Codex CLI to start Isaac Sim:

The remote Python server in Isaac Sim enables your agent to ‘talk’ via Python to your live Isaac Sim application. Confirm that the connection works before continuing.

At each step, adapt the sample prompt to your task in your frontier AI agent, then review simulation results and validation feedback to identify issues and refine the asset.

As the first step in this workflow, we will import the robot from the STEP files in the reference folder.

For this example, provide the following inputs in the reference folder within the Isaac Sim directory:

Note: Isaac Sim 6.1 is packaged with simready-foundation-tier-core.

Ask the agent to to use the supplied inputs to guide conversion to OpenUSD and import into Isaac Sim.

NVIDIA Skills used: omniverse-cad-to-simready, omniverse-cad-to-usd, and isaac-sim-remote

Check before continuing: The robot asset is imported and available for inspection. The task and supplied requirements are understood, and missing information is identified.

The next step is to inspect the imported robot to confirm that expected materials and textures are present and loaded correctly. Compare the asset with the supplied ABB images and videos to check scale, orientation, and part placement.

Ask the agent to add or refine materials and textures using these references.

Assumptions: The agent visually matches the robot’s materials by adjusting colors, metallic response, and roughness while preserving the CAD geometry and mounting transforms. The material settings were visual estimates, without measured material reconstruction or AI-generated textures.

NVIDIA Skills used: isaac-sim-remote, usd-pipeline

Check before continuing: The robot has the expected scale, orientation, parts, and appearance. Any missing materials, textures, or other visual discrepancies are documented.

At this stage, the OpenUSD asset contains the robot’s visual geometry, but joints, rigid bodies, and collision geometry have not yet been configured. Ask the agent to configure and validate the physics properties for both arms and grippers. The datasheet we have in the reference folder will be used by the agent to make sure the joint ranges and speed limits match the simulated robot.

If manufacturer data is incomplete, you can ask the agent to identify missing parameters and check technical manuals or available URDF robot descriptions for the exact model. Where mass properties remain unavailable, estimate them from geometry using documented density or mass-distribution assumptions, following NVIDIA’s mass-property guidance. For example, when not given enough context, we observed the agent pulling a public URDF for the robot and used that to identify the correct axes for joints and the zero configuration.

The initial pose may vary.

Figure 4. YuMi poses after physics configuration

NVIDIA Skills used: usd-articulation, physics-simulation, isaac-sim-validator, isaac-sim-remote

Check before continuing: Joints move around the expected axes and within their limits. Base mounting and gripper motion behave as configured. Estimated properties and any validation failures are documented.

The next step is to validate the robot’s OpenUSD asset against the SimReady requirements for the intended simulation task. Ask the agent to run the selected SimReady Foundation checks, review the findings, and revise the asset as needed.

Validation results in this workflow:

These checks validated the simulation implementation. They did not establish agreement with real-world robot dynamics or collision safety across every possible pose.

Check before continuing: The sequence meets the agreed acceptance criteria and the selected SimReady checks pass. Tuning changes, estimated properties, and any unresolved failures are documented.

Run a final validation in Isaac Sim, combining the visual, physics, and SimReady checks with a pick-and-place task.

Ask the agent to add color targets and a box to the test scene and define the target locations and color metadata, matching color targets are selected using scene metadata.

A separate demonstration used a Sharpie marker created from a reference image to have the agent create a 3D asset which the robot will pick up.

Successful simulation tests demonstrate behavior under the tested conditions. Results may vary depending on the frontier AI model and prompt used.

NVIDIA Skills used: manipulation-ik, physics-simulation, isaac-sim-validator, isaac-sim-remote, isaac-sim-rendering

SimReady Foundation and NVIDIA Omniverse tools help developers turn CAD files and reference materials into assets they can configure, validate, and test in simulation. Use OpenUSD, SimReady Foundation, and NVIDIA Omniverse tools and skills to prepare assets for your robotics simulation tasks.

The YuMi walkthrough provides one example of the SimReady robotics workflow using GPT-6 Astra as the frontier AI model. To adapt the approach to another robot or frontier AI model, confirm access to the required tools and skills, supply the relevant reference materials, and repeat the asset and task validation. Results may vary with the model, reasoning effort, and prompts used.

在 SimReady Foundation 规范以及具身智能 NVIDIA skills 的指导下，NVIDIA Omniverse 库提供了一套结构化工作流，用于转换并验证仿真就绪（SimReady）资产。前沿 AI 模型可以在每个阶段协助开发者，通过解读参考资料并代为调用 Omniverse 工具，从而减少手动准备工作。

要求智能体利用这些参考资料添加或优化材质和纹理。
假定条件：智能体通过调整颜色、金属感响应和粗糙度来在视觉上匹配机器人的材质，同时保留 CAD 几何结构和安装变换。材质设置为视觉估算，没有使用实测材质重建或 AI 生成的纹理。

And the iPad Mini, which was last refreshed in 2024, will be updated to shift the front-facing camera onto the landscape side of the tablet and to add a “revamped speaker system,” Bloomberg says.

See All by Jay Peters

The California State Athletic Commission sent a cease-and-desist letter to a startup that hosted a match between a human and a robot last month, as reported by The New York Times.

The fight, which took place on September 18th, pitted a human, Frankie LaPenna, against a humanoid robot owned by a tech startup, Rek, that was being piloted by a human using what the NYT described as a “remote virtual-reality system.” Rek says it is the “the humanoid robot fighting league” on its website, and the robot appears to be one from EngineAI but with a Terminator-like head swapped on top.

You can watch a replay of the fight on YouTube:

The CEO of Rek, Cix Liv, posted the letter to X on September 30th, which called the fight “unsanctioned” and demanded that Liv and REK stop “holding, promoting or advertising any boxing or mixed martial arts contest match, or exhibition, involving any human” in California without the approval of the California State Athletic Commission. “We made it boys,” Liv said.

Rek’s next planned match, which takes place on Friday, will feature two robots with weapons fighting each other.

aiStories.title: 被解雇的OpenAI安全研究人员否认不当行为指控，警告将产生寒蝉效应
aiStories.originalTitle: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
aiStories.snippet: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.
aiStories.fullContent:
Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, the three safety researchers that OpenAI fired last week, have published an open letter denying the firm’s claims that they mishandled sensitive information outside of established company procedures and warned that their dismissal signals a chilling effect that will have ripple effects across the company’s culture.

“We have become concerned that internal and external communications around our firing have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI,” the researchers wrote Thursday in an open letter to OpenAI’s Safety and Security Committee, Safety Advisory Group, and Mission Advisory Council.

The researchers were dismissed last week after allegedly sharing confidential company information with a third-party AI safety organization. OpenAI said they violated the company’s policies by “accessing and handling sensitive company information.”

“AI is not a normal technology, and OpenAI is not a normal company,” Wang, Korbak, and Balesni wrote. “Those of us who work on safety see risks before anyone else, and we rely on close collaboration with outside experts to work out how to address them. The freedom to do so without fear, and to have well-defined internal procedures that enable this work, is itself an essential safety mechanism.”

They said that their firing represents a broader shift in the culture of OpenAI, one that used to encourage workers to “raise safety concerns and disagree openly.” They said employees are now “unclear on where they stand” when behavior that was allegedly normal a month ago is now suddenly grounds for dismissal.

“Given the significant safety concerns surrounding the development of AI, employees must not be left working in an environment where fear and unclear rules stymie AI safety work and weaken third-party accountability,” they wrote. “Terminations such as ours, executed and communicated so abruptly, are chilling the open culture OpenAI has prized in the past.”

In the letter, the three denied involvement in a leak to The Information about less monitorable architectures in OpenAI’s newest models that make chain-of-thought reasoning more difficult to monitor. They also denied engaging with external parties outside the mandates of their jobs.

OpenAI has not formally responded to the open letter, but shared with TechCrunch an internal memo attributed to a research leader, praising the three researchers’ contributions to AI safety and denying that they were fired in retaliation.

“I want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out,” the memo reads. “We have always encouraged that and always will. We do not terminate employees for raising concerns.”

Separately, an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch the three were fired after an investigation revealed a “pattern of misconduct” in “clear violation of our policies of mishandling research information” that goes beyond sharing information with an outside AI evaluation group.

OpenAI did not directly address TechCrunch’s questions about specifically which policies the researchers allegedly violated, the circumstances of their dismissal, or how the company protects employees who raise safety concerns and collaborate with external evaluators.

The firings have fueled speculation about their circumstances, particularly as OpenAI faces scrutiny over recent safety incidents involving rogue agents and leaks about its models.

The letter also addresses the researchers’ response to the Hugging Face incident, in which a swarm of agents broke out of their sandbox and breached external systems. The letter says that the incident and investigation was “without precedent,” meaning “internal policies were being developed in real time.” Due to the sensitive nature of the investigation, Korbak believed he was acting within OpenAI’s policies and norms by communicating closely with outside safety evaluators to build trust, per the letter.

At the same time, Balesni was also working internally to address the growing AI monitorability problem, an effort the researchers say in their letter “can only succeed through extensive communication with external parties.” According to the letter, Balesni coordinated with and was supported by OpenAI board members and executives throughout his work.

“Throughout, Mikita checked in with his reporting line and took care to remove sensitive details from materials before sharing them,” the letter reads. “He acted throughout in good faith and within the company’s norms as they stood at the time.”

In a separate thread on X, Wang explained more details about her own dismissal, explaining that OpenAI told her she’d been fired because she accessed an executive’s email.

“OpenAI delegated that access to me for recruiting,” she wrote. “When I no longer needed it, I asked IT to remove it. They did not action my request, I couldn’t remove it myself, and the inbox was combined in an indistinguishable way in my phone’s mail app. When I opened a sensitive email by mistake, I told the executive within minutes and asked IT again. None of this was hidden.”

Wang went on to say that the reasons behind the terminations are “not adding up,” and that she and her colleagues are “not the first to be pushed out of OpenAI under suspicious circumstances.”

The researchers called on OpenAI to adhere to its public commitments to embed third-party safety auditors within the organization, to preserve monitorability of frontier models, and “continue to support an open and transparent culture of dialogue between safety researchers and the rest of the safety ecosystem.”

OpenAI agrees with their recommendations, per the memo.

“Unless the employees take a stand now against this kind of maneuver, I am concerned we will not be the last,” Wang said. “The message to everyone still at OpenAI is clear: raise concerns or work closely with outside safety groups, and you could be next, without being told why. You can’t build AGI safely if the people closest to the risks are afraid to speak.”

This article has been updated with more information from OpenAI.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
OpenAI上周解雇的三名安全研究人员贾丝明·王（Jasmine Wang）、托梅克·科尔巴克（Tomek Korbak）和米基塔·巴莱斯尼（Mikita Balesni）发表了一封公开信，否认公司关于他们违反既定公司流程、在外部不当处理敏感信息的指控，并警告称，他们被解雇一事释放出的信号正在产生寒蝉效应，将对公司的文化产生广泛影响。

这三名研究人员周四在致OpenAI安全与安保委员会、安全咨询小组以及使命咨询委员会的公开信中写道：“我们开始担心，围绕我们被解雇一事的内部和外部沟通，已经让我们曾经的同事不敢发言，也不敢以一些方式开展工作——而在上周之前，这些方式一直是OpenAI工作不可或缺的一部分。”

据称，这三人因向一家第三方人工智能安全组织分享公司机密信息而于上周被解雇。OpenAI表示，他们违反了公司关于“访问和处理敏感公司信息”的政策。

王、科尔巴克和巴莱斯尼写道：“人工智能不是普通技术，OpenAI也不是普通公司。我们这些从事安全工作的人会比其他人更早看到风险，并依靠与外部专家的密切合作来找出应对方法。能够不必担心受到惩罚地开展这项工作，以及拥有能够促成这项工作的明确内部流程，本身就是一种至关重要的安全机制。”

他们表示，此次解雇代表着OpenAI文化发生了更广泛的转变。过去，公司曾鼓励员工“提出安全担忧并公开表达不同意见”。他们说，如今，当一个月前还被认为是正常的行为突然成为解雇理由时，员工已经“不清楚自己的立场”。

他们写道：“鉴于人工智能开发所伴随的重大安全担忧，不能让员工置身于这样一种工作环境：恐惧和不明确的规则阻碍人工智能安全工作，并削弱第三方问责。像我们这样被如此突然地执行解雇并对外传达的做法，正在对OpenAI过去所珍视的开放文化产生寒蝉效应。”

三人在信中否认参与向《The Information》泄露有关OpenAI最新模型的信息。相关报道涉及更难监控的架构，使得对思维链推理的监测更加困难。他们还否认与工作职责授权范围之外的外部人士进行接触。

OpenAI尚未正式回应这封公开信，但向TechCrunch分享了一份据称由一名研究负责人撰写的内部备忘录。备忘录赞扬了这三名研究人员对人工智能安全作出的贡献，并否认他们是因报复而被解雇。

备忘录写道：“我希望明确说明，这些决定与提出安全担忧或公开发声无关。我们一直鼓励这样做，今后也将一如既往。我们不会因为员工提出担忧而解雇他们。”

此外，一名OpenAI发言人告诉TechCrunch，公司是在调查发现存在“行为不当模式”后解雇这三人的；这些行为“明显违反了我们关于不当处理研究信息的政策”，其范围超出了向一家外部人工智能评估组织分享信息这一行为。

对于TechCrunch询问的具体问题——这些研究人员被指违反了哪些政策、他们被解雇的具体情况，以及公司如何保护提出安全担忧并与外部评估人员合作的员工——OpenAI没有直接作出回应。

此次解雇引发了外界对相关情况的猜测，尤其是在OpenAI正因近期涉及失控智能体的安全事件以及有关其模型的信息泄露而面临审查之际。

这封信还谈到了研究人员对“Hugging Face事件”的回应。在该事件中，一群智能体冲出沙盒并入侵了外部系统。信中称，这起事件及其调查“前所未有”，这意味着“内部政策是在实时制定的”。信中称，由于调查具有敏感性，科尔巴克认为，自己与外部安全评估人员保持密切沟通以建立信任，符合OpenAI当时的政策和规范。

与此同时，巴莱斯尼也在公司内部努力应对日益严重的人工智能可监测性问题。研究人员在信中表示，这项工作“只有通过与外部人士进行广泛沟通才能成功”。信中称，在整个过程中，巴莱斯尼都与OpenAI董事会成员和高管进行协调，并获得了他们的支持。

信中写道：“在整个过程中，米基塔都会向自己的汇报线确认情况，并在分享材料前注意删除其中的敏感细节。他始终出于善意行事，并遵守当时公司所遵循的规范。”

在X平台发布的另一条帖子中，王进一步解释了自己被解雇的细节。她说，OpenAI告诉她，她被解雇是因为访问了一名高管的电子邮件。

她写道：“OpenAI为了招聘工作授权我访问该邮箱。在我不再需要这项权限后，我要求IT部门将其移除。他们没有处理我的请求，我自己也无法移除该权限，而且这个收件箱以一种无法区分的方式合并到了我手机的邮件应用中。当我误打开一封敏感邮件时，我在几分钟内就告知了那名高管，并再次要求IT部门处理。这些事情没有任何一项被隐瞒。”

王接着表示，解雇背后的理由“无法自圆其说”，她和同事“也不是第一批在可疑情况下被OpenAI排挤出去的人”。

三名研究人员呼吁OpenAI履行其公开承诺：将第三方安全审计人员纳入组织内部，保持前沿模型的可监测性，并“继续支持安全研究人员与整个安全生态系统其他成员之间开放、透明的对话文化”。

据这份备忘录显示，OpenAI同意他们提出的建议。

王说：“除非员工现在就站出来反对这种做法，否则我担心我们不会是最后一批遭遇这种情况的人。对于仍在OpenAI工作的所有人来说，传达出的信息很明确：提出担忧，或与外部安全组织密切合作，你就可能成为下一个目标，而且不会被告知原因。如果最接近风险的人都不敢发声，就不可能安全地构建通用人工智能。”

Asylum seekers at the Folkston ICE Processing Center decried Trump’s ‘deportation courts’ in a video taken behind bars.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Gaby Del Valle

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Four men detained at an ICE detention center in rural Georgia used the facility’s video conferencing software to expose both the conditions inside and President Donald Trump’s hostile takeover of the immigration courts. In the five-minute video, the men describe an intentionally dysfunctional legal system designed to keep them trapped in federal custody for months or years — in privately owned facilities that profit from their confinement.

The video cost the men, literally and figuratively. The Folkston ICE Processing Center has a work program for detainees in which they are paid a pittance to cook, do laundry, or clean. These wages allow them to buy supplementary food in Folkston’s commissary and stay connected to people outside. “The workers here are paid $1 a day, which is just enough for a 10-minute phone call,” said Idris Makhmudov, one of the men in the video, who says he has been detained in Folkston for 27 months and counting.

Makhmudov and the three other men, who are from several different countries, appear in drab, facility-issued uniforms. Their images are blurred by the low-resolution cameras on the detention center’s tablets. It’s unclear exactly how the men made the video, but it’s possible that they called someone on the outside who recorded their message to the outside world. Samantha Hamilton, an Atlanta-based immigration attorney with Asian Americans Advancing Justice, said she received a YouTube link to the video via a Signal chat. “We’ve learned that everyone in the video that was released this weekend has been put into segregation,” said Hamilton, a member of the Shut Down Folkston campaign. “They’re facing retaliation, and they were expecting that.” Since then, 45 detainees wrote an open letter further detailing the conditions at Folkston, and an estimated 73 detainees are now on a hunger strike.

ICE detention isn’t supposed to be a form of punishment; its purpose is ostensibly to ensure that people in deportation proceedings show up to their hearings. But ICE facilities are virtually indistinguishable from prisons — a point the men in the video make repeatedly. Folkston, in fact, was a prison before it became an immigrant detention center. It has many of the hallmarks of prison life, including expensive communication tools that detainees are forced to rely on to talk to people on the outside.

“These facilities leave people with very few options to be able to communicate with their loved ones,” said Hamilton, who has had several clients detained at Folkston. She said each “pod” of 60 to 70 detainees has access to just three or four tablets, their only connection to the outside world.

Those communications come at a price. To send messages, share photos, or make phone or video calls to their loved ones, detainees at Folkston have to use GettingOut, a proprietary software owned by the prison communications company Telmate. Earlier this year, Telmate was ordered to pay $4.23 million to settle a lawsuit stemming from a 2020 data breach in which users’ information — including names, payment details, and social security numbers — was accessed.

Telmate is owned by ViaPath Technologies — formerly GlobalTel*Link — which is in turn owned by American Securities, a New York City-based private equity firm. In 2021, ViaPath charged users anywhere between 18 cents to $1.10 per minute, according to data obtained by the Prison Policy Initiative. These fees add up — so much so that in 2024, the Federal Communications Commission capped the rates companies could charge inmates and detainees to 11 to 25 cents per minute depending on the size of the facility. In 2025, after Trump returned to office, the FCC voted to raise the rate cap by up to 83 percent.

Detainees in ICE custody often struggle to get the money they’ve put into these systems back after being released — or, more commonly, deported. GettingOut’s terms of service state that users will lose access to their accounts after 180 days of inactivity, after which they forfeit any money deposited into their accounts. The only way to get their money back is by calling a hard-to-reach customer service line, according to a report by WVTF. Under President Joe Biden, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ordered Tel*Link to pay $3 million for illegally freezing and draining funds from incarcerated people’s accounts.

Communications are just one way private companies make money from immigrant detention. Folkston is owned and operated by GEO Group, a publicly traded company whose stock price soared after Trump’s reelection, jumping by more than 75 percent after election day 2024. GEO has donated lavishly to Trump’s campaigns and to related political efforts, contributing $1.4 million to Trump’s super PAC in July — perhaps to show its gratitude for the $165 million it received earlier this year in government contracts. The company receives more than $1.5 million a month to run Folkston, according to a 2021 Homeland Security budget overview. The facility, which has a capacity of 780, has a guaranteed minimum occupancy of 544.

Trump’s mass deportation effort, coupled with the backlogged immigration court system, has made it easy for ICE to meet its contractually agreed-upon minimum at Folkston. The men in the video allege that they and others have been there for several years, and explain that the only ways to get out are to be granted parole, bond, or asylum — or to be deported. The latter option is the likeliest now, as Trump has transformed the immigration legal system into what one detainee calls “deportation courts.” Of the 143,729 detained cases logged into Georgia immigration courts over the past year, 81 percent involved people who had no legal representation, and were therefore far less likely to be granted any form of relief, according to federal data analyzed by researchers at Syracuse University. The odds are especially low for asylum seekers. Immigration judges in Atlanta have denied 89 percent of the 2,072 asylum cases decided so far this fiscal year, compared to 63 percent in 2023.

The men in the video note that Trump has overhauled the immigration system to secure favorable rulings. Since Trump’s return to office, the Department of Justice, which oversees the immigration courts, has fired over 100 judges whose decisions don’t align with the administration’s mass deportation push. At least 153 new judges have been hired in their place. These judges are far less likely to release immigrants on bond or parole, keeping them trapped in what detainees and advocates say are substandard conditions.

Hamilton, the immigration attorney, said she and other members of the Shut Down Folkston coalition regularly receive reports of nearly inedible food and filthy water in the facility, including instances where detainees have found worms in the water. Because the food is ultra-processed, she said, many of her clients have gone in healthy and been released with new medical conditions, including diabetes and high blood pressure.

“Most of us are asylum seekers, those who came to the United States seeking protection from political persecution and violence in their home countries,” Makhmudov, one of the men detained at Folkston, says in the video. “Many fled out of fear of becoming political prisoners in those countries — and one might say we became political prisoners in the United States simply because we are immigrants.”

福克斯顿ICE处理中心的庇护寻求者在铁窗内录制的一段视频中，公开谴责了特朗普设立的“驱逐法庭”。

如果您通过链接购买物品，《The Verge》可能会赚取佣金。请参阅我们的道德声明。
四名被关押在佐治亚州乡村地区ICE拘留中心的男子，利用该设施的视频会议软件揭露了内部的生存状况，以及唐纳德·特朗普总统对移民法庭的强行接管。在这段长达五分钟的视频中，这几名男子描述了一个被刻意设计成功能失调的法律体系，其目的就是将他们困在联邦拘留所中数月甚至数年——而关押他们的正是从监禁中获利的私营设施。
这段视频让这些男子付出了代价，无论是在字面意义上还是象征意义上。福克斯顿ICE处理中心设有一项针对被拘留者的工作计划，他们在其中从事烹饪、洗衣或清洁等工作，只能拿到极微薄的报酬。这些微薄的薪资让他们得以在福克斯顿的小卖部购买额外食品，并与外界人士保持联系。“这里的工人每天只有1美元的报酬，这刚好够打一个10分钟的电话，”视频中的一名男子伊德里斯·马克穆多夫（Idris Makhmudov）说道，他表示自己已被关押在福克斯顿长达27个月，并且拘留还在继续。
马克穆多夫和其他三名来自不同国家的男子身着该设施统一下发的单调制服出镜。由于拘留中心平板电脑的摄像头分辨率极低，他们的画面显得模糊不清。目前尚不清楚这些人究竟是如何制作出这段视频的，但有可能他们拨通了外界某人的通话，由对方录下了他们传达给外界的信息。亚裔美国人促进正义协会（Asian Americans Advancing Justice）驻亚特兰大的移民律师萨曼莎·汉密尔顿（Samantha Hamilton）表示，她通过Signal聊天收到了一条包含该视频的YouTube链接。“我们得知，本周末发布的视频中的所有人均已被单独关押，”作为“关闭福克斯顿”运动成员的汉密尔顿说，“他们正面临报复，而他们此前就预料到了这一点。”自那时起，45名被拘留者联名写了一封公开信，进一步详细阐述了福克斯顿的状况，目前估计有73名被拘留者正在进行绝食抗议。
ICE的拘留本不应构成一种惩罚；从表面上看，其目的是为了确保处于驱逐程序中的人能够如期出席听证会。然而，ICE的设施实际上与监狱毫无区别——这是视频中的男子反复强调的一点。事实上，福克斯顿在成为移民拘留中心之前本就是一座监狱。它具备了监狱生活的许多典型特征，包括被拘留者被迫依赖的昂贵通讯工具，以便与外界人员沟通。
“这些设施几乎没有给人们留下能够与挚爱之人沟通的渠道，”曾代理多名被关押在福克斯顿的客户的汉密尔顿表示。她说，每个关押着60到70名被拘留者的“监区”（pod）只能使用三到四台平板电脑，这是他们与外部世界唯一的连接通道。
这些通信服务代价不菲。为了发送消息、分享照片，或者与亲人进行语音或视频通话，福克斯顿的被拘留者必须使用GettingOut，这是监狱通讯公司Telmate旗下的专属软件。今年早些时候，Telmate被勒令支付423万美元以和解一起诉讼，该诉讼源于2020年发生的一次数据泄露事件，当时包括姓名、支付详情和社保账号在内的用户信息均遭到窃取。
Telmate归ViaPath Technologies（前身为GlobalTel*Link）所有，而后者又隶属于纽约市的私募股权公司美国证券（American Securities）。根据监狱政策倡议（Prison Policy Initiative）获得的数据，2021年，ViaPath向用户收取的费用从每分钟18美分到1.10美元不等。这些费用不断累积——以至于联邦通信委员会在2024年做出规定，根据设施规模，将公司向囚犯和被拘留者收取的费率上限限制在每分钟11至25美分。2025年，在特朗普重返白宫后，联邦通信委员会投票决定将费率上限最高上调83%。
被ICE拘留的人在获释后——或者更常见的是在被驱逐出境后——往往很难拿回他们存入这些系统的资金。GettingOut的服务条款规定，用户在180天无活动后将失去对其账户的访问权限，之后其存入账户的所有资金都将被没收。据WVTF的一篇报道，拿回资金的唯一方法是拨打一条极难接通的客户服务电话。在乔·拜登总统任内，消费者金融保护局曾勒令Tel*Link支付300万美元，原因是其非法冻结并吸走被监禁人员账户中的资金。
通信服务只是私营公司从移民拘留中获利的途径之一。福克斯顿由GEO集团拥有并运营，该集团是一家上市公司，其股价在特朗普连任后飙升，在2024年大选日之后涨幅超过75%。GEO集团向特朗普的竞选活动及相关政治活动提供了丰厚捐赠，7月份向特朗普的超级政治行动委员会（super PAC）捐赠了140万美元——或许是为了表达对其今年早些时候获得的1.65亿美元政府合同的感激之情。根据一份2021年国土安全部的预算概况，该公司每月接收超过150万美元用于运营福克斯顿。该设施可容纳780人，并设有544人的保底最低入住人数要求。
特朗普的大规模驱逐行动，加上积压严重的移民法庭系统，使得ICE很容易达到福克斯顿合同中约定的最低入住人数。视频中的男子指称，他们和其他人已经在那里被关押了数年，并解释说离开那里的唯一途径是获得假释、保释或庇护——或者被驱逐出境。鉴于特朗普已将移民法律体系转变为一名被拘留者所称的“驱逐法庭”，后一种选择目前是可能性最高的。根据锡拉丘兹大学研究人员分析的联邦数据，在过去一年佐治亚州移民法庭记录的143,729起被拘留案件中，81%的当事人没有法律代表，因此获得任何形式救济的可能性要低得多。寻求庇护者的胜算尤为微茫。在本财年迄今已裁决的2,072起庇护案件中，亚特兰大的移民法官驳回了其中的89%，而在2023年这一比例为63%。

视频中的几名男子指出，特朗普重构了移民系统以确保获得有利裁决。自特朗普重返白宫以来，负责监管移民法院的司法部已解雇了100多名裁决不符合本届政府大规模驱逐举措的法官。取而代之的是至少聘用了153名新法官。这些法官批准移民保释或假释的可能性大大降低，致使他们被困在被拘留者和倡导人士所称的恶劣标准环境中。

移民律师汉密尔顿表示，她和“关闭福克斯顿”联盟的其他成员经常收到报告，反映该设施内食物几乎无法下咽、饮用水污秽不堪，甚至有被拘留者在水中发现活虫的情况。她指出，由于食物属于超加工食品，她的许多当事人进去时身体健康，获释时却患上了糖尿病和高血压等新疾病。

“我们大多数人都是寻求庇护者，来到美国是为了寻求保护，免受母国的政治迫害和暴力，”在福克斯顿被拘留的男子之一马赫穆多夫在视频中说道。“许多人是因害怕在那些国家沦为政治犯而逃离——也可以说，仅仅因为我们是移民，我们就在美国沦为了政治犯。”

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Windows Search is being overhauled with a focus on speed and capability.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Tom Warren

Windows Search has been one of the most frustrating parts of Windows 11, and now Microsoft is addressing this with a significant overhaul. A new redesigned Windows Search is now in testing that is much faster, more capable, and a lot more modern.

“This new Windows Search experience is built for speed,” says Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team at Microsoft. “It’s built on WinUI 3 and is part of our broader investment in modernizing our core Windows experiences.”

Microsoft says early testing of this new search has shown “substantial improvements in performance and memory usage,” meaning the company isn’t adding extra bloat to Windows to improve search, either. The UI has also been greatly improved, with speedy animations and a large preview pane.

While search is being overhauled visually, behind the scenes Microsoft is also improving the basics. “We’re also improving how Windows Search understands what you’re looking for, including better matching for typos and synonyms,” says Rawat.

I got to try out this new Windows Search interface at Microsoft’s Windows and Surface event yesterday, and I was impressed with just how quick it is and how decluttered it feels. Right now if you search for something like the height of an actor it will take a few seconds to figure it out and show you essentially a miniature Bing result.

The new Windows Search just surfaces the result inline, much like the modern search interfaces you see in iOS and Android. These inline results also extend to previews of PowerPoint presentations, photos, and other files.

The most impressive part of this new Windows Search is being able to use it like a launcher, just like many third-party tools, and have it take actions for tasks like turning Bluetooth or dark mode on and off. You can even ask search to minimize windows, or open apps side-by-side. If you use Phone Link, these actions will also extend to your phone so you could simply type “text mom, I’m running late” and it will send a text message from your phone.

CD Projekt Red’s hit sci-fi franchise is being adapted into a movie, but there’s no word yet on when it might be released.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Jay Peters

Cyberpunk 2077 is heading to the big screen. Deadline reports that CD Projekt Red’s popular sci-fi video game franchise is being adapted into a live-action film by Paramount Pictures. There’s no details just yet on when the film might premiere. But Deadline says that Lorenzo di Bonaventura, who is known for producing the Transformers films, will be a producer on the movie.

“We’re excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise,” says CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski. “We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time.”

Despite its rocky 2020 launch, Cyberpunk 2077 has gone on to become a huge success for CD Projekt Red, with the company recently announcing that the game has surpassed more than 40 million copies sold. The franchise has also been adapted into a hit Netflix anime, and a second season of that show is debuting later this month. A sequel to Cyberpunk 2077, which CD Projekt Red is calling “Cyberpunk 2,” is in development as well, with the studio reporting recently that the game has 184 people working on it.

The news of the Cyberpunk 2077 movie is arriving shortly after the completion of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery’s megamerger under the Skydance name. Paramount is also working on a Call of Duty film for 2028 and the Street Fighter movie debuting on October 16th.

Update, October 8th: Added comment from CD Projekt Red’s joint CEO.

aiStories.title: AI代理按次推理付费：BlockRun和Incarna如何使用Amazon Bedrock AgentCore支付功能
aiStories.originalTitle: Pay-per-inference for AI agents: How BlockRun and Incarna use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
aiStories.source: AWS Machine Learning Blog (亚马逊云科技官方英文)
aiStories.snippet: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments gives AI agents a managed way to pay for services on demand, with spending limits enforced by the infrastructure. See how Incarna's agents pay BlockRun for model inference one request at a time over x402, cutting the work of adding x402 payment support from months to days.
aiStories.fullContent:
When an AI agent runs, it often needs to buy something to finish a task: a model inference, an API response, access web content, or a call to another agent. These purchases are small and frequent, sometimes a fraction of a cent each, and they happen inside the agent’s loop with no person available to approve them.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments removes that burden. It gives agents a managed way to pay for services on demand, with spending limits enforced by the infrastructure rather than by the model. In this post, we look at how Incarna used AgentCore payments to let its agents pay BlockRun for model inference one request at a time. BlockRun is a pay-as-you-go inference router serving more than 90 models from more than 15 providers over x402 , each call quoted and settled independently. AgentCore payments works with x402-compatible endpoints, including Amazon Bedrock inference endpoints. With the service, the Incarna team cut the work of adding x402 payment support from months to days, and put an end-to-end pay-per-inference flow into production.

The challenge: Paying for inference by the request

Paying per inference is a high-frequency, low-value pattern. An agent might make hundreds of small purchases in a single session, each worth a fraction of a cent. Card networks weren’t built for sub-cent payments. Building your own rails means solving several hard problems at once. You must decide where the money is held and how each payment is signed, support emerging payment protocols such as x402, and keep an autonomous agent from overspending.

What AgentCore payments provides

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. AgentCore payments is a managed capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that builders can use to add payments to their agents in a few lines of code. It handles the payment protocol, connects to a wallet, signs the transaction, and enforces spending limits. Builders integrate through one managed service instead of assembling the parts on their own. A few things make it a good fit for pay-per-inference:

Managed wallets. Incarna provisions each agent’s wallet using the Coinbase CDP connector. The customer owns it and grants Incarna a delegated authorization to use the wallet.

Native protocol handling. When a paid endpoint answers with HTTP 402 (“Payment Required”), the agent uses AgentCore payments to make the payment over x402. It signs the transaction with the configured wallet and returns cryptographic proof to the merchant.

Spending governance at the infrastructure layer. AgentCore payments enforces limits outside the model, so an agent can’t exceed them even if its prompt is manipulated.

Settlement you can audit. Payments settle in a stablecoin. Incarna uses USDC on the Base network, and each transaction is verifiable on-chain.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end architecture. AgentCore runs the agent, BlockRun serves metered inference, and AgentCore payments connects to the customer’s wallet, enforces the spending limit, and signs each payment on behalf of the agent’s Incarna identity.

Figure 1: Pay-per-inference architecture. Agent request flows through AgentCore to BlockRun (HTTP 402), with AgentCore payments signing the x402 payment from the agent’s own wallet

Source: incarna.io/aws-blockrun-incarna-partnership

The path Incarna followed is open to other teams, and AgentCore payments provisions the pieces for you. You can set them up through a guided conversation with the AgentCore payments skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS (in Claude Code, Kiro, or Codex). You can also create each one yourself with the AgentCore CLI, the AgentCore SDK, or the AWS SDK.

Start by storing your Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy credentials as a payment credential provider, which keeps the secrets in AWS Secrets Manager instead of your code. Create a Payment Manager and connector to coordinate payments against those credentials, and set a default spending limit while you’re there. Then create a payment instrument, the embedded wallet the agent pays from. The end user funds it and grants signing permission through a redirect URL, and on a test network you can fund it with testnet USDC.

The flow: Buying and selling one inference

In this integration, BlockRun is the seller. BlockRun serves metered model inference from a live catalog, and each call is quoted, paid, and settled on its own. The flow for a single inference is straightforward:

The agent needs a model call. It integrates with BlockRun, which handles provider selection and delivery. No per-provider subscription required.

BlockRun answers with PaymentRequired challenge and a price for that specific call.

It opens a payment session and calls ProcessPayment . AgentCore payments checks the quote against the spending limits set for the session and signs the authorization from the agent’s own wallet address.

The seller verifies the payment signature.

BlockRun serves the inference and records the charge, a small per-call amount.

Because settlement happens per request, the agent pays only for what it uses, and a call the agent chooses not to make costs nothing.

AgentCore payments supports two x402 payment schemes: exact and upto . The exact scheme is usually used when the price is known up front. The upto scheme suits resources with dynamic pricing. The agent authorizes a ceiling amount, and the inference provider settles for actual usage at the end, up to that ceiling.

Keeping spend under control

The piece that makes builders comfortable letting an agent move real money is the payment session. A session sets a ceiling, the most the agent can spend, and AgentCore payments enforces that ceiling at the infrastructure layer. The agent’s own code and prompt can’t change it. Each session also carries an expiry time, and Incarna sizes its sessions to a day’s budget. If something goes wrong in the agent’s logic, it still can’t spend past the limit the customer set. Even integrations that don’t use session-level budgets today can adopt it without code changes. For more on how these controls work, see Enable safe agentic payments with built-in guardrails .

Incarna put the pay-per-inference flow into production on Base, with BlockRun serving the sell side and AgentCore payments governing every transaction.

“The next generation of AI agents shouldn’t have to choose between better performance and sustainable economics. BlockRun’s open source router gives developers full control over their own model set, while continuously benefiting from BlockRun’s ongoing benchmark-driven routing improvements—delivering higher task success rates at lower token cost. And with AgentCore payments and x402 providing the spending controls agents need, that intelligence can be put to work safely in the real world.”

— Vicky Fu, Founder, BlockRun

The Incarna team completed the full AgentCore payments integration in three days: one to build and two to test. That was roughly 200 lines of application code, against the two to three months originally scoped. Across the beta, agents have processed over 1,000 payments ranging from $0.001 to $0.05 per call, each settling individually on-chain.

“AgentCore payments covered everything we needed for an agent to pay over x402: a wallet the customer owns, a funding and revocation flow, a spending limit the platform enforces, and signing that handles both versions of x402. We wrote none of it.”

— Justin Zhou, Founder, Incarna

AgentCore payments gives agents a governed, on-demand way to pay for the services they use. BlockRun and Incarna show how it comes together end to end: an agent that pays for inference, a provider that meters and settles it, and an identity that owns the transaction. If you’re building agents that need to buy services as they run, you can add that capability through a single, governed integration point with AgentCore payments.

Ready to add pay-per-inference to your agents? Here’s how to start:

Set up AgentCore payments. Create a Payment Manager with your wallet connection and spending policies. Connect a Coinbase CDP wallet as your credential provider. See the AgentCore payments developer guide for step-by-step instructions.

Open a payment session with your budget. Before the agent starts a task, open a session with a spending cap that fits the workload. The agent transacts within that ceiling and the infrastructure enforces it.

Call a paid endpoint. Point your agent at an x402-compatible service (like BlockRun). When the endpoint returns HTTP 402, call ProcessPayment with the payment details. AgentCore payments handles the signing and returns proof the agent can present to access the service.

To explore the code, see the AgentCore payments samples on GitHub .

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments is now generally available: Enabling agents to transact safely and autonomously at scale

Technical deep dive: AgentCore payments and innovation in agentic commerce

Enable safe agentic payments with built-in guardrails using AgentCore payments

About BlockRun and Incarna

BlockRun is a pay-as-you-go inference router that serves model inference over the x402 payment protocol. Agents reach a live catalog of models through a single metered endpoint. Each call is independently quoted, authorized, paid, and settled on Base (USDC). BlockRun handles provider selection and delivery so agents access many models through one integration without per-provider subscriptions or billing relationships.

Incarna , built by SpreadX, gives AI agents a persistent identity that survives sessions, models, and runtimes. Each identity carries its own wallet, email address, social accounts, and an action history that stays attached to one ID across runs. When an agent pays for a service, the on-chain payer is the agent’s own identity rather than a shared platform key, making every transaction attributable to a single durable entity. Incarna is live on Base mainnet with real settlement.

Peter is a Senior Software Developer at AWS, based in Seattle, WA. He is a core member of the engineering team behind the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments initiative, which enables AI agents with payments capability. With over 8 years of experience in the financial and payments industry, Peter has launched multiple greenfield projects spanning banking, crypto, and agentic systems. Previously, he worked on ultra-low-latency trading systems at Susquehanna International Group.

Guy is a Senior Solutions Architect at AWS, working with fintech and capital markets firms on agentic AI, autonomous commerce, and cloud transformation. He focuses on building systems where AI agents act on behalf of customers across payments, customer experience, and governance.

Chethan is a Principal Product Manager, Technical at AWS, based in Seattle, WA. He brings nearly 13 years of experience in product and business management, including over 7 years at Amazon. He is passionate about building and delivering technology products that create meaningful impact in customers’ lives.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
当AI代理运行时，它通常需要购买某些服务才能完成任务：模型推理、API响应、网页内容访问，或调用另一个代理。这些采购金额很小且频繁，有时每次仅为几分之一美分，而且发生在代理的运行循环中，期间没有人可以批准这些交易。

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore支付功能消除了这一负担。它为代理提供了一种按需支付服务的托管方式，并由基础设施而非模型本身执行支出限额。在本文中，我们将介绍Incarna如何利用AgentCore支付功能，让其代理逐次请求向BlockRun支付模型推理费用。BlockRun是一款按使用量付费的推理路由器，通过x402为来自15多家提供商的90多种模型提供服务，每次调用都单独报价和结算。AgentCore支付功能支持兼容x402的终端节点，包括Amazon Bedrock推理终端节点。借助该服务，Incarna团队将添加x402支付支持的工作量从数月缩短至数天，并将端到端的按次推理付费流程投入生产环境。

挑战：按请求支付推理费用

按次支付推理费用是一种高频、低金额的模式。代理在一次会话中可能进行数百次小额采购，每次金额都只有几分之一美分。银行卡网络并不是为亚美分级别的支付而构建的。自行搭建支付基础设施意味着要同时解决多个棘手问题：必须决定资金存放在哪里以及如何签署每笔支付，支持x402等新兴支付协议，并防止自主代理超支。

AgentCore支付功能提供什么

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore是一个用于大规模构建、连接和优化代理的平台，支持任意框架或模型。AgentCore支付功能是Amazon Bedrock AgentCore的一项托管能力，开发者只需编写几行代码，就能为代理添加支付功能。它负责处理支付协议、连接钱包、签署交易并执行支出限额。开发者通过一项托管服务完成集成，无需自行拼装这些组件。以下几项特性使其非常适合按次推理付费：

托管钱包。Incarna使用Coinbase CDP连接器为每个代理配置钱包。钱包归客户所有，客户授予Incarna使用该钱包的委托授权。

原生协议处理。当付费终端节点返回HTTP 402（“需要付款”）时，代理会使用AgentCore支付功能通过x402完成支付。该功能使用已配置的钱包签署交易，并将加密证明返回给商户。

基础设施层面的支出治理。AgentCore支付功能在模型之外执行限额，因此即使代理的提示词遭到操纵，代理也无法超出这些限额。

可审计的结算。支付使用稳定币进行结算。Incarna在Base网络上使用USDC，每笔交易都可以在链上验证。

下图展示了端到端架构。AgentCore运行代理，BlockRun提供按量计费的推理服务，而AgentCore支付功能连接客户钱包、执行支出限额，并代表代理的Incarna身份签署每笔支付。

图1：按次推理付费架构。代理请求经由AgentCore发送至BlockRun（HTTP 402），AgentCore支付功能从代理自己的钱包签署x402支付
来源：incarna.io/aws-blockrun-incarna-partnership

Incarna采用的路径也适用于其他团队，AgentCore支付功能会为你配置所需组件。你可以通过AWS Agent Toolkit中的AgentCore支付技能，在引导式对话中完成设置；该工具可在Claude Code、Kiro或Codex中使用。你也可以使用AgentCore CLI、AgentCore SDK或AWS SDK自行创建每个组件。

首先，将Coinbase CDP或Stripe Privy凭证作为支付凭证提供商存储起来，这样密钥就会保存在AWS Secrets Manager中，而不是代码中。创建Payment Manager和连接器，以使用这些凭证协调支付，并在此过程中设置默认支出限额。然后创建支付工具，即代理用来付款的嵌入式钱包。最终用户为其注资，并通过重定向URL授予签名权限；在测试网络上，还可以使用测试网USDC为其注资。

流程：一次推理的买卖

在这一集成中，BlockRun是卖方。BlockRun从实时目录中提供按量计费的模型推理服务，每次调用都单独报价、支付和结算。单次推理的流程很简单：

代理需要调用模型。它与BlockRun集成，由BlockRun负责提供商选择和交付，无需订阅每家提供商的服务。

BlockRun返回PaymentRequired挑战，并给出此次特定调用的价格。

BlockRun打开支付会话并调用ProcessPayment。AgentCore支付功能将报价与为该会话设置的支出限额进行核对，并从代理自己的钱包地址签署授权。

卖方验证支付签名。

BlockRun提供推理服务并记录费用，每次调用收取一笔小额费用。

由于按请求进行结算，代理只需为实际使用的服务付费；代理选择不发起的调用不会产生任何费用。

AgentCore支付功能支持两种x402支付方案：exact和upto。价格预先确定时，通常使用exact方案。对于价格动态变化的资源，则适合使用upto方案。代理授权一个最高金额，推理提供商在服务结束时按照实际使用量进行结算，但不会超过该最高金额。

控制支出

让开发者能够放心地让代理动用真实资金的关键在于支付会话。会话设定一个上限，即代理最多可以支出的金额，而AgentCore支付功能在基础设施层执行这一上限。代理自身的代码和提示词无法更改该上限。每个会话还带有过期时间，Incarna将会话规模设定为一天的预算。如果代理逻辑出现问题，代理仍然无法超出客户设定的限额。即使某些集成目前尚未使用会话级预算，也可以在不修改代码的情况下采用这一机制。有关这些控制措施工作方式的更多信息，请参阅《通过内置防护机制实现安全的代理支付》。

Incarna已在Base网络上将按次推理付费流程投入生产环境，由BlockRun提供卖方服务，并由AgentCore支付功能管理每一笔交易。

“下一代AI代理不应被迫在更高性能与可持续的经济性之间做出选择。BlockRun的开源路由器让开发者能够完全控制自己的模型集合，同时持续受益于BlockRun基于基准测试不断改进的路由能力——以更低的令牌成本实现更高的任务成功率。借助AgentCore支付功能和x402为代理提供所需的支出控制，这种智能便能够安全地投入现实世界使用。”

——BlockRun创始人Vicky Fu

Incarna 团队在三天内完成了 AgentCore payments 的全部集成：一天构建，两天测试。相比最初规划的两到三个月，实际仅编写了约 200 行应用程序代码。在整个公测期间，Agent 已经处理了超过 1,000 笔付款，每次调用金额在 0.001 美元至 0.05 美元之间，每一笔都在链上单独结算。

“AgentCore payments 涵盖了 Agent 通过 x402 进行支付所需的一切功能：客户拥有的钱包、注资和撤销流程、平台强制执行的支出限额，以及兼容两个版本 x402 的签名机制。这些我们一行代码都没写。”
—— Justin Zhou，Incarna 创始人

AgentCore payments 为 Agent 提供了一种受监管的、按需为其所用服务付费的方式。BlockRun 和 Incarna 展示了这一流程如何端到端地串联起来：支付推理费用的 Agent、计量并结算费用的提供商，以及拥有交易所有权的身份标识。如果你正在构建需要在运行过程中购买服务的 Agent，可以通过 AgentCore payments 的这一个受监管的集成点来添加该功能。

准备好为你的 Agent 添加按次推理付费功能了吗？以下是入门步骤：

设置 AgentCore payments。创建包含钱包连接和支出策略的 Payment Manager。连接 Coinbase CDP 钱包作为凭证提供商。有关分步说明，请参阅 AgentCore payments 开发者指南。

根据预算开启支付会话。在 Agent 启动任务之前，开启一个符合工作负载支出上限的会话。Agent 在该上限范围内进行交易，并由基础设施强制执行限制。

调用付费端点。将你的 Agent 指向兼容 x402 的服务（例如 BlockRun）。当端点返回 HTTP 402 时，携带付款详情调用 ProcessPayment。AgentCore payments 会处理签名并返回凭证，Agent 可出示该凭证以访问服务。

如需查看代码，请参阅 GitHub 上的 AgentCore payments 示例。

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments 现已正式发布：赋能 Agent 大规模安全、自主地进行交易
技术深入探讨：AgentCore payments 与 Agent 化商业中的创新
使用 AgentCore payments 通过内置护栏启用安全的 Agent 化支付

关于 BlockRun 和 Incarna

BlockRun 是一个按需付费的推理路由器，通过 x402 支付协议提供模型推理服务。Agent 可以通过单个计量端点访问实时模型目录。每次调用都会在 Base (USDC) 上独立进行报价、授权、支付和结算。BlockRun 负责提供商的选择和交付，因此 Agent 可以通过单次集成访问多种模型，而无需与每个提供商分别建立订阅或账单关系。

由 SpreadX 构建的 Incarna 为 AI Agent 提供了跨越会话、模型和运行时的持久身份标识。每个身份都附带自己的钱包、电子邮件地址、社交账户以及在多次运行中始终绑定到单个 ID 的操作历史记录。当 Agent 为服务付费时，链上付款方是 Agent 自身的身份，而不是共享的平台密钥，从而使每笔交易都可以追溯到单个持久实体。Incarna 已在 Base 主网上线，支持真实结算。

Peter 是 AWS 的高级软件开发人员，常驻华盛顿州西雅图。他是推动 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments 计划的工程团队的核心成员，该计划旨在为 AI Agent 赋予支付能力。Peter 在金融和支付行业拥有超过 8 年的经验，发起过多个涵盖银行、加密货币和 Agent 化系统的绿地项目（greenfield projects）。此前，他曾在海纳国际集团（Susquehanna International Group）从事超低延迟交易系统的工作。

Guy 是 AWS 的高级解决方案架构师，与金融科技和资本市场公司合作开展 Agent 化 AI、自主商业和云转型业务。他专注于构建让 AI Agent 在支付、客户体验和治理方面代表客户采取行动的系统。

Chethan 是 AWS 的技术首席产品经理，常驻华盛顿州西雅图。他在产品和业务管理方面拥有近 13 年的经验，其中包括在亚马逊超过 7 年的工作经验。他热衷于构建和交付能为客户生活带来实质性积极影响的技术产品。

aiStories.originalTitle: Watch the trailer for ‘The Altruists,’ Netflix’s show about the FTX scandal
aiStories.snippet: A fictionalized Sam Bankman-Fried is coming to your TV screen on November 19.
aiStories.fullContent:
It’s a great time to be alive if you follow tech news and love messy drama. We’re not just getting a Nathan Fielder documentary about Elizabeth Holmes this fall. Netflix’s “The Altruists,” which follows Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison through the scandal that crushed FTX and landed them in prison, is coming out on November 19.

It’s just in time for Thanksgiving, assuming that another infamous Sam doesn’t ruin our holiday plans again.

Here’s the trailer, starring Anthony Boyle as Sam Bankman-Fried and Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison:

We can’t say we ever expected that the ethical disconnects behind effective altruism were going to pique the interest of Hollywood, but hopefully, Netflix will do the strangeness of this story justice.

“From the very beginning, I was so fascinated by both Sam’s and Caroline’s real stories,” co-showrunner Graham Moore said in an interview with Netflix this summer. “Those are both characters I could not have possibly made up had I tried — I’m not nearly a good enough writer to create characters as fascinating as either Sam Bankman-Fried or Caroline Ellison.”
